data_source: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), LOLA Altimeter DEMs, LROC NAC Imagery, LEND Neutron Spectrometer, Diviner Radiometer, LCROSS Impact Results
data_references: Mazarico et al. (2011) – LOLA Illumination Modeling, Icarus 211
Zuber et al. (2012) – LOLA Topographic Maps, Nature 486
Sanin et al. (2017) – LEND Hydrogen Mapping, Icarus 283
Colaprete et al. (2010) – LCROSS Impact Water Detection, Science 330
NASA (2022) – Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions, nasa.gov
NASA (2023) – Refined 9 Artemis III Landing Regions, nasa.gov
Gläser et al. (2018) – Illumination Analysis, Planetary & Space Science 162
target_region: Lunar South Pole (84°S – 90°S), Artemis Candidate Landing Regions
coordinate_datum: Moon_IAU2000 Sphere (R = 1737.4 km), Elevation relative to 1737.4 km reference

landing_sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
landing_sites.description: 21 km impact crater at the south pole. Rim peaks receive near-continuous sunlight while the interior holds one of the deepest PSRs with confirmed water ice signatures.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Extremely High – Proximity to shadowed water ice; PSR floor may contain billions of years of volatile record

landing_sites.name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton–De Gerlache)
landing_sites.description: Elevated ridge between Shackleton and De Gerlache craters. Highest modeled illumination of any lunar surface point – up to 95.7% at 10 m mast height per Gläser et al. (2018).
landing_sites.scientific_value: Very High – Premier solar power site; adjacent to both Shackleton and De Gerlache PSRs

landing_sites.name: De Gerlache Rim 1
landing_sites.description: Northern rim of the heavily shadowed De Gerlache crater. Crater floor never sees sunlight and harbors high hydrogen concentrations per LEND data.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Very High – Highest shallow ice concentration among rim sites; deep PSR volatile reservoir

landing_sites.name: De Gerlache Rim 2
landing_sites.description: Southern elevated rim zone overlooking De Gerlache crater. Strategic access to both sun-visibility patches and adjacent polar ice reservoirs. Part of NASA's refined 9 candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – Access to deep PSR ice; challenging but scientifically rewarding terrain

landing_sites.name: De Gerlache-Kocher Massif
landing_sites.description: Mountainous massif between De Gerlache and Kocher craters. Elevated terrain provides favorable illumination above surrounding crater floors.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – Massive geological diversity; ancient SPA basin material exposed

landing_sites.name: Malapert Massif
landing_sites.description: Prominent mountain ridge at ~86°S. Excellent direct line-of-sight to Earth for communication relay. One of NASA's refined 9 Artemis III candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – Ideal communication relay; best Earth-facing site for permanent infrastructure

landing_sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
landing_sites.description: Western rim of Nobile crater at ~85.3°S. One of NASA's refined 9 Artemis III candidate regions. Relatively smooth highland terrain suitable for rover traverses.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Very High – VIPER rover target region; smooth terrain with accessible volatile deposits

landing_sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
landing_sites.description: Eastern rim of Nobile crater. Analyzed via GIS-MCDM algorithms as an optimal site balancing safety, sunlight, and volatile access. Part of NASA's refined 9 candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – Geologically diverse rim; optimal rover access to crater floor volatiles

landing_sites.name: Faustini Rim A
landing_sites.description: Rim of the ancient, heavily degraded Faustini crater. Interior PSR is one of the coldest measured surfaces on the Moon (as low as 25 K per Diviner). Extensive hydrogen enrichment.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – One of the coldest PSRs; extremely stable ice environment; large volatile floor area

landing_sites.name: Haworth Crater Rim
landing_sites.description: Large crater adjacent to Shackleton. Interior PSR sustains ultra-cold temperatures. Part of NASA's refined 9 Artemis III candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Very High – Massive PSR area; strong neutron suppression indicates deep ice reserves

landing_sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
landing_sites.description: Broad flat-topped plateau near the south pole. Unusually smooth for the polar region. Part of NASA's refined 9 Artemis III candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Moderate – Safest terrain; ideal for first crewed landing; limited but accessible volatiles nearby

landing_sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
landing_sites.description: Elevated plateau on the SPA basin rim. Among the original 13 Artemis candidate regions. Ancient crustal material exposed by basin-forming impact.
landing_sites.scientific_value: High – SPA basin rim geology; crustal stratigraphy exposed; ancient impact melt samples

landing_sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B
landing_sites.description: Elevated peak adjacent to Cabeus crater, where LCROSS confirmed 5.6% water ice by mass in 2009. Part of NASA's refined 9 Artemis III candidate regions.
landing_sites.scientific_value: Extremely High – LCROSS ground-truth site; confirmed 5.6 wt% water ice; highest confidence volatile deposit
